X-FACTOR AI tool literacy: You actively use AI tools such as Claude, Gemini, or equivalents to accelerate research, content drafting, and course development. The Lead Field Engineer - Transmission Lines , will provide field engineering support for the Transmission Construction projects, with a primary focus on steel transmission line construction. Working directly with construction teams, contractors, project managers, utility clients, quality assurance and multidisciplinary engineering teams, this role will provide technical engineering reviews, site supervision, and timely field decisions to support safe, quality, and efficient construction. The successful candidate will be a decisive and collaborative Professional Engineer with strong transmission line and foundation knowledge, capable of evaluating changing field conditions, resolving technical issues, and making sound engineering decisions in active construction environments. This is a field-based position requiring frequent travel to remote construction sites throughout British Columbia and work in variable terrain and weather conditions. Primary Responsibilities Providing field engineering support during transmission line construction, including foundations, civil works, steel tower assembly and erection, conductor and OPGW stringing, grounding, insulators, hardware and associated line components; Monitoring construction quality and conformance with approved drawings, specifications, standards and project requirements, and identifying deficiencies or non-conforming work requiring corrective action; Providing technical guidance to field crews and contractors on transmission line construction matters while maintaining clear distinction between engineering requirements and the contractor’s responsibility for construction means, methods and site safety; Participating in daily construction meetings, look-ahead planning, sequencing and constructability discussions to proactively identify and resolve engineering constraints; Monitoring construction progress from an engineering perspective and identifying technical issues, decisions or information gaps that may affect schedule, productivity, quality or safety; Collaborating with civil, structural and electrical engineering teams on foundation, tower, line hardware, access and other multidisciplinary field issues; Evaluating unexpected site conditions including terrain, geotechnical conditions, weather-related impacts and structural or constructability constraints, and developing practical engineering solutions; Supporting technical review of construction methodologies and temporary requirements where they may affect the permanent design assumptions or engineering integrity; Exercising professional judgment and independent decision-making within approved design criteria, and escalating issues where required based on technical risk, scope, or authority. Qualifications 10+ years of relevant engineering experience, preferably including significant transmission line construction and field engineering experience; University Bachelor's degree in Civil, Structural or Electrical Engineering; Civil or Structural Engineering is preferred; Registered as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) with Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia (EGBC), or eligible for immediate registration; Demonstrated transmission line design and/or foundation engineering experience is required; Previous field engineering, construction support, or site supervision experience on transmission line projects is strongly preferred; Experience with steel transmission tower foundations, assembly, erection, conductor and OPGW stringing, insulators, hardware accessories and fittings; Strong understanding of civil and foundation construction, including excavation, concrete, anchors, geotechnical conditions, drainage, access, and constructability considerations; Familiarity with transmission line industry standards and guidelines including applicable CSA requirements and relevant NESC, IEC, IEEE, ASCE and CIGRE standards and practices; Strong professional judgment with the ability to assess incomplete or changing field information, make timely decisions and communicate clear engineering direction; Demonstrated ability to identify non-conforming work, evaluate technical risk, determine appropriate corrective action, and make decisions at inspection hold points; Sound understanding of project management systems and the relationship between engineering decisions, construction sequencing, schedule, quality, and project risk; Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to coordinate effectively with multidisciplinary field crews, contractors, project teams, and utility clients; Self-motivated and collaborative, with the ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities and remain effective in a fast-paced construction environment; Valid Canadian Driver’s License and willingness to travel frequently and work at remote or active construction sites throughout British Columbia; Job Description Our client is seeking a Construction Manager to lead on-site field execution for the Rock Island Arsenal Power Generation and Microgrid project for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) at Rock Island Arsenal, Illinois. The project includes power generation, medium-voltage distribution, battery energy storage, controls and cybersecurity, civil, mechanical, and commissioning work across multiple operating companies and subcontractors. Serving as the on-site superintendent with authority to act for the contractor, the Construction Manager is responsible for coordinating all field activities, integrating subcontractors and delivery teams, and ensuring the project is completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and in compliance with quality and contract requirements. Working closely with the Project Manager, CQC System Manager, SSHO, Project Controls/Scheduler, and Document Control team, this role applies established field execution standards and delivery processes from mobilization through final acceptance. Day to Day: · On-Site Superintendence: Serve as the QGS superintendent on the worksite at Rock Island Arsenal throughout performance of the work, with the authority to direct the work and act for QGS, and lead in a way that keeps QGS satisfactory to the Contracting Officer. · Field Execution: Manage the day-to-day execution of the work, directing field operations, operating company crews, subcontractors, and trades so work is completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with the plans and specifications. · Operating Company and Subcontractor Integration: Integrate the work of all Quanta operating companies and subcontractors across electrical (medium voltage distribution, switchgear, generators, and battery energy storage), civil and duct bank, structural, fire suppression, mechanical and gas, controls and cybersecurity, and testing and commissioning scopes into one coordinated field plan, managing interfaces, sequencing, laydown, and site logistics. · Safety Leadership: Champion QGS safety programs and a zero-incident culture, and enforce EM 385-1-1, the Accident Prevention Plan, and Activity Hazard Analyses in the field in partnership with the SSHO. · Quality Control Support: Support the CQC System Manager in executing the USACE three-phase control process (preparatory, initial, and follow-up phases), testing, and deficiency correction, while respecting the independence of the CQC function. · Schedule and Look-Ahead Planning: Provide field input to the cost-loaded Primavera P6 project schedule in coordination with the Senior Project Controls Specialist/Scheduler, lead weekly look-ahead planning with the operating companies and subcontractors, verify actual progress reported each period, and develop field recovery plans when work falls behind. · Daily Reporting and Documentation: Ensure daily production and field reporting is accurate, complete, and entered in RMS on time in coordination with the Document Control/RMS Admin, and maintain field records that support quality, safety, progress, and pay estimate documentation. · Submittals, RFIs, and Changes: Coordinate the field side of submittals, RFIs, and field changes with the Project Manager, confirm approved submittals are in place before work proceeds, and identify differing site conditions and potential changes early so they can be raised with the Government in accordance with the contract. · Government and Installation Coordination: Serve as the primary field interface with the USACE Resident or Area Office, Government quality assurance representatives, and installation stakeholders, coordinating site access, work hours, planned outages, and utility tie-ins with the Project Manager. · Site Compliance: Enforce installation access, security, environmental (including stormwater and spill response), and federal labor requirements on site. · Testing, Commissioning, and Closeout: Coordinate field execution of acceptance testing and commissioning with the commissioning agent, testing firms, and manufacturer representatives, and drive punch list completion, final inspections, and Government acceptance. Job Type: Full-time, Direct Placement Opportunity Yearly Salary: $160,000-$210,000 Workplace Type: On-site in Rock Island, Illinois
